topicTitle: 4.3 Least Common Multiple of Algebraic Expressions
stem:
(a) Find the HCF of the following monomials by completing the table.
| Monomials | HCF of numerical coefficients | HCF of variables (each) | Required HCF |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| $16 \mathrm{p}^{3} \mathrm{q}, 9 \mathrm{pq}^{2} \mathrm{r}$ |  |  |  |
| $10 p^{3} q^{2} r, 5 p^{2} q r, 15 p^{2} q r^{2}$ |  |  |  |
| $14 p^{4} q r^{4}, 28 p^{3} q r^{2}, 7 p^{2} q r^{2}, 21 p^{2} q^{2} r^{4}$ |  |  |  |
(b) If all common factors with least power of three unknown polynomials are $2^{2}, 3, \mathrm{pq}$ and $(p+q)^{2}$ then what would be their HCF?
(c) Write any two polynomials of your choice having HCF as 1.
(d) The only common factor of two polynomials is m-n and the only uncommon factor is $\mathrm{m}^{2}+\mathrm{n}^{2}$. Can you guess the unknown polynomials?
(e) Can you guess HCF of two polynomials $x^{3}+5 x+1$ and $1+5 x+x^{3}$ without any procedure?
keyPoints: ["HCF takes the lowest power of every common factor","Identical polynomials have themselves as HCF","Coprime polynomials have HCF equal to $1$"]
modelAnswer:
(a) Row 1: numerical HCF of $16$ and $9$ is $1$; variables give $pq$; required HCF $=pq$.
Row 2: numerical HCF of $10,5,15$ is $5$; least powers give $p^{2}qr$; HCF $=5p^{2}qr$.
Row 3: numerical HCF of $14,28,7,21$ is $7$; least powers give $p^{2}qr^{2}$; HCF $=7p^{2}qr^{2}$.
(b) HCF $=2^{2}\\cdot3\\cdot pq\\cdot(p+q)^{2}=12pq(p+q)^{2}$.
(c) For example $x$ and $x+1$, which share no factor.
(d) The polynomials could be $(m-n)$ and $(m-n)(m^{2}+n^{2})$, since the common factor is $m-n$.
(e) The two polynomials are identical, so their HCF is $x^{3}+5x+1$ itself.

topicTitle: 4.3 Least Common Multiple of Algebraic Expressions
stem:
Find the HCF of the following by factorization.
$(a-b)^{3}, a^{2}-2 a b+b^{2}$
keyPoints: ["Lowest power of the common factor wins"]
modelAnswer:
$a^{2}-2ab+b^{2}=(a-b)^{2}$, so the expressions are $(a-b)^{3}$ and $(a-b)^{2}$.
HCF $=(a-b)^{2}$.

stem: If HCF and LCM of two polynomials are $x-7$ and $x^{3}-10 x^{2}+11 x+70$ respectively. Then find product of two polynomials.
modelAnswer:
Product of the two polynomials $=$ HCF $\times$ LCM
$=(x-7)(x^{3}-10x^{2}+11x+70)$.

stem: Product of two polynomials is $x^{4}+3 x^{3}-12 x^{2}-20 x+48$ and their HCF is $x-2$. Find their LCM.
keyPoints: ["Divide the product by the known factor"]
modelAnswer:
LCM $=\frac{\text{product}}{\text{HCF}}=\frac{x^{4}+3x^{3}-12x^{2}-20x+48}{x-2}$.
Synthetic division by $2$ gives quotient $x^{3}+5x^{2}-2x-24$ with zero remainder.
LCM $=x^{3}+5x^{2}-2x-24$.

stem: The product of two polynomials is $y^{4}+6 y^{3}-3 y^{2}-56 y-48$ and their LCM is $y^{3}+2 y^{2}-11 y-12$. Find their HCF.
keyPoints: ["Product divided by LCM gives the HCF"]

stem: Find the second polynomial when, First polynomial $=x^{4}+x^{3}+x+1, \mathrm{HCF}=x+1$ and $\mathrm{LCM}=\left(x^{3}+1\right)\left(x^{4}+x^{3}-x-1\right)$
modelAnswer:
Second polynomial $=\frac{(x+1)\left(x^{3}+1\right)\left(x^{4}+x^{3}-x-1\right)}{x^{4}+x^{3}+x+1}$.
Since $x^{4}+x^{3}+x+1=(x+1)(x^{3}+1)$, everything cancels except one factor:
second polynomial $=x^{4}+x^{3}-x-1$.

stem: Find the LCM of polynomials $4 x^{3}-10 x^{2}+4 x+2$ and $3 x^{4}-2 x^{3}-3 x+2$ if their HCF is $x-1$.
keyPoints: ["Check that the given HCF actually divides both polynomials"]
modelAnswer:
$4x^{3}-10x^{2}+4x+2=2(x-1)(2x^{2}-3x-1)$ and $3x^{4}-2x^{3}-3x+2=(x-1)(3x^{3}+x^{2}-x-2)$.
Each contains exactly one factor $(x-1)$, matching the given HCF.
LCM $=\frac{\text{product}}{x-1}=2(x-1)(2x^{2}-3x-1)(3x^{3}+x^{2}-x-2)$.
